# Artifact Keeper 1.11.5

A maintenance release on the 1.11 line: 10 changelog entries from 10 pull requests since 1.11.4, all backported from `main`. The headline is **virtual conda channels keep serving while they rebuild** (#4879, #4881): a virtual channel used to drop its merged repodata as soon as a remote member's cache expired, so every request waited on a full rebuild (about 45 seconds for a conda-forge `linux-64` `.bz2`) and a client refreshing a dozen subdirs at once got `503` and timeouts. It also ran a separate merge for each of `repodata.json`, `.json.zst` and `.json.bz2`. Now one subdir is merged once for every encoding, the previous document is served while exactly one background merge rebuilds it, and an `AK_PROXY_METADATA_BUDGET_BYTES` above 4 GiB is honoured, so the default merge concurrency grows with it. Next to it, **a CRAN remote repository now proxies the upstream `PACKAGES` index** (#4877), so R clients pointed at one can install packages at all. Around them are replication fixes (chunked generic uploads reach push peers, NuGet and nested RPM writes no longer echo, pacman signatures and conda attestations added later reach peers), a failed hosted Maven upload that no longer leaves downloadable bytes, repository delete removing older revisions' objects, a remote conda CEP-16 shard that recovers once its upstream does, a `400` for a plugin git redirect the SSRF policy refuses, and the `startup` series of `ak_db_pool_connection_failures_total` on `/metrics`. **No schema migrations.** One new setting, `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_MAX_STALE_SECS`, which defaults to the merge cache TTL. No security advisories ship with this release.

## Read this first: what now answers with an error or refuses

- **A plugin install or reload whose git source redirects to a blocked address answers `400`, not `500`** (#4869). The outbound SSRF policy refuses a host that resolves to a blocked address ("blocked by SSRF policy") and a redirect hop that points at one ("redirect target rejected by SSRF policy"). Only the first wording was recognized when a plugin git clone failed, so a source that redirected onto a blocked address fell through to the internal-error branch. Both refusals are now classified through one shared vocabulary: the plugin install and reload paths answer `400` with the policy wording, as the connect-time refusal already did, and an upstream proxy fetch whose redirect the policy refuses is reported as `503` instead of a generic `500`. No security change: the redirect is still aborted before the target is contacted.
- **A hosted Maven jar or pom with no catalog row answers `404` instead of being served from storage** (#4837). A hosted Maven upload stores its file before the transaction that records it, so when that transaction failed (a metadata write error, a quota refusal, a failed POM read) the client got an error while the object stayed in storage, and on object storage the repository's storage fallback then served the rejected deploy. The upload now removes its object when the publish does not commit, on every storage backend, and the fallback serves only the row-less files it exists for (checksum sidecars and `maven-metadata.xml`). A client that relied on downloading a coordinate whose publish had failed now gets `404`. The cleanup is serialised against an overlapping upload of the same coordinate, so a failed upload can never delete the bytes of a concurrent one that succeeds.

## Read this second: behaviour that changes without an error

- **A virtual conda channel merges each subdir once for every encoding and serves the previous merged repodata while it rebuilds** (#4879). The merged `repodata.json` is now kept once, zstd-encoded, and `.json` and `.bz2` are derived from it on first demand and kept with it; each encoding keeps its own ETag. When a kept document is no longer fresh it is served at once with a `Warning: 110 - "Response is Stale"` header while exactly one background merge rebuilds it, and the next request after the rebuild gets the new document, with the encodings the previous one had been asked for already built. Stale serves count as `ak_conda_virtual_merge_cache_hits_total{via="stale"}`. A merge with a failed member is never served stale, and the CEP-16 shard index is never served stale. **`CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_MAX_STALE_SECS`** bounds how long after it was first found stale a document may still be served; it defaults to the merge cache TTL (`CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_CACHE_TTL_SECS`, 300 by default), and `0` restores waiting on the rebuild. Two things operators may notice: the plain `.json` of a virtual channel is now compact JSON instead of pretty-printed, and `repodata.json.sig` signs the derived `.json` bytes, so it still verifies against what `.json` serves. A kept document now stays in the merge cache for its TTL plus the stale window; see `docs/operations/conda-virtual-merge-memory.md` for sizing.
- **A CRAN repository of type `remote` proxies the upstream `PACKAGES` / `PACKAGES.gz` index** (#4877). The source index was built from locally-catalogued rows alone, and a proxy repository only has rows for packages already fetched through it, so `GET /cran/{repo}/src/contrib/PACKAGES` answered an empty `200` even though the upstream publishes a full index, and `install.packages()` had nothing to resolve against. A remote repository now fetches the upstream `src/contrib/PACKAGES` (falling back to `PACKAGES.gz` for mirrors that ship only the gzipped form) and merges it over the locally-held rows, keeping every upstream field (`Depends`, `Imports`, `LinkingTo` and the rest) because R resolves the dependency graph from them. A locally-held package still wins its `(Package, Version)` slot. An upstream that publishes no index (`404`) is not an error, but a genuine upstream failure with nothing held locally is now reported as an error instead of an empty `200`.
- **Chunked uploads through `/api/v1/uploads` replicate to subscribed push peers** (#4791). The chunked finalize path wrote its own `artifacts` row and never queued a push sync task, so a completed chunked upload reached a peer only after a manual sync. It now fans out like every direct and format-native publish, and a write that arrived from a peer is not pushed out again.
- **NuGet and nested-layout RPM writes no longer echo between peers, and a pacman signature or conda attestation added after its package reaches push peers** (#4792). The NuGet push handler and the nested RPM upload (`repodata_depth > 0`) queued push sync tasks even for a write that arrived from a peer, so it was pushed back out to every push peer of the repository; both now skip the fan-out. A pacman `.sig` and a conda CEP-27 attestation are stored in their package's metadata, and attaching one queued nothing, so a peer that already had the package never got it. Attaching one now delivers the package again with its new metadata, including when the push was still in flight. On the receiving side, a trusted peer pushing the exact bytes already live at a path is accepted as a replay that refreshes the metadata, instead of being refused with `409`. Client uploads of identical bytes to an occupied coordinate are still refused, and a peer still cannot change the bytes of a released coordinate. A peer on an older release keeps refusing the replay, so it receives the signature or attestation only after it is upgraded.
- **A remote conda channel serves a CEP-16 shard again once its upstream does** (#4829). Since 1.11.0 a shard whose upstream bytes do not hash to its address is answered with `502`, but those bytes had already been written to the proxy cache under a path cached as immutable, so the remote, and every virtual over it, kept answering `502` for that shard until the entry was evicted by hand. A shard is now checked against its address before it is cached, and a mismatched shard stored by an earlier release is evicted on the next request and fetched again, so an affected cache heals without operator action. Both cases count in `ak_proxy_cache_checksum_mismatch_total`.

## Read this third: operations and logging

- **`AK_PROXY_METADATA_BUDGET_BYTES` above 4 GiB is honoured instead of silently clamped** (#4881). The buffered-metadata budget counted one permit per byte through an API limited to 32-bit counts, so an operator who set 32 GiB got a 4 GiB budget, and the default `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MAX_CONCURRENT_MERGES` derived from it stayed at 3. The budget is now accounted in 4 KiB units (a reservation rounds up to a whole unit), so 32 GiB yields `budget_bytes: 34359738368` and 28 default merges at the default member ceilings. A blank, non-numeric or zero value still falls back to the 1 GiB default, and that, or a value too large to represent, now logs a warning at startup naming the configured and effective values.
- **Deleting a versioned Generic or MLModel repository removes the objects of its older revisions** (#4865). The delete collected storage keys only from the repository's live artifacts. Older revisions live in `artifact_versions`, whose rows cascade away with the repository, so the history objects stayed on filesystem and object storage and the storage GC orphan scan could never find them. The delete now covers live artifacts and revisions under the same sharing guard, and a revision key it spares because another repository still names it is handed to the storage-GC candidate set, so the next GC pass reclaims it once no reference remains. Space already orphaned by earlier deletes is not recovered by this change.
- **`ak_db_pool_connection_failures_total{stage="startup"}` is exported** (#4828). The startup connect retry added in 1.11.2 counted every failed initial connect attempt, but the database pool was built before the Prometheus recorder was installed, so the `startup` series never appeared on `/metrics`. The recorder is now installed first, so a replica that needed several attempts to reach the database reports them once it is up. The `request` series was not affected, and metric names and labels are unchanged.

The full entries are in the `## [1.11.5]` section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.5/CHANGELOG.md).
